title: indigo_agent_mount: a sync refused by the mount driver can be reported as successful
description:
Found on 2026-11-18 while working on ticket 37fc5504-1588-420f-9da1-0f15ba5d6f3f (the mount base driver now refuses a sync within 5 degrees of the celestial pole with MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES in ALERT and a message).

Observation from reading the Mount Agent, not yet reproduced by a test: after it requests a sync it can treat the operation as done when the published coordinates are within its tolerance (0.25 degrees) of the requested ones, and the ALERT state of the refusal is overwritten by the next position poll of the driver (OK with the unchanged real coordinates). A sync requested close to the current pointing can therefore be reported as successful although the driver refused it and no alignment point was added; callers such as the plate-solver sync and center flow would continue as if the model had been updated.

To do: first reproduce with an automated test against mount_simulator (sync refused near the pole, requested coordinates within the tolerance of the pointing) and record what the agent reports; then make the agent fail the sync when the driver answered the request with ALERT, without changing the drivers' published coordinates. Update the agent version and its tests.

Owner decision (2026-11-19): the agent-side fix is not the right solution. The systemic way for a mount driver to publish coordinates from its position poll is indigo_update_coordinates(); that function is the single place that must handle 'the property is ALERT and has to stay ALERT'. A mount driver whose poll does not publish through indigo_update_coordinates() is defective. Survey: mount_synscan publishes MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES from the poll with indigo_update_property() and never calls indigo_update_coordinates(); ioptron, lx200, nexstar, nexstaraux, pmc8, rainbow, starbook, temma set OK in the driver before publishing; mount_simulator leaves the state alone.

indigo_update_coordinates() takes the state the driver wrote into the property, so it cannot tell a poll's OK from the OK of a successful request. What releases a kept ALERT: (a) only the next client request on MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES and a BUSY state, with every ALERT kept, including one from a failed readback; or (b) the same, but an ALERT published without a message by the poll (failed readback) is not kept and the next good poll restores OK?

BLOCKING
1. indigo_drivers/agent_mount/indigo_agent_mount.c:1640 - a stale ALERT republished by an idle poll is taken as the answer to a new sync, so a sync that the mount accepted (alignment point added) is reported 'Mount refused the sync' / 'Sync failed'. mount_simulator (position_handler idle branch, indigo_mount_simulator.c:181-189) and LX200 (meade_update_mount_state, indigo_mount_lx200.driver:3660-3676) keep MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES in ALERT across polls after any refusal/failure (pole refusal, 'Too many alignment points', failed GoTo, aborted slew). Sequence: earlier operation leaves ALERT -> agent sync: line 413 clears the flag, line 414 sets pending, line 415 sends the request -> a poll publishes the old ALERT before the driver processes the request -> line 1641 sets mount_goto_alert -> driver accepts the sync and publishes OK -> line 510 fails it. In-process the window is only the microseconds between line 414 and the synchronous change_property, so practically unreachable; with the agent and the mount on different servers every ALERT update sent by the server within about one RTT of the request arrives after pending=true, i.e. a probability of roughly RTT / poll interval (1 s for both drivers) per sync that follows a lingering ALERT. Unlike mount_goto_accepted, which is protected by matching the target, the ALERT carries nothing that identifies the request. Required fix: count only a transition into ALERT, e.g. 'if (CLIENT_PRIVATE_DATA->mount_goto_pending && property->state == INDIGO_ALERT_STATE && CLIENT_PRIVATE_DATA->mount_eq_coordinates_state != INDIGO_ALERT_STATE)'; mount_eq_coordinates_state is assigned only at line 1659, so it still holds the previous state there. A refusal on a mount whose ALERT persists still fails through the existing final-state check (state != OK); synscan resets to OK within 0.2 s, far less than the agent's 3 s wait between syncs, so its refusal is still a transition OK->ALERT. Both existing cases keep passing. Adjust the comment at 1639 accordingly.

NON-BLOCKING
- Suggested regression case (mount simulator): sync that is refused because the requested dec > 85 while the mount points below 85, then a sync near the real pointing must be 'Synced' (covers the flow logic; the network race itself is not deterministically reproducible in-process).
- The 'mount simulator: sync refused near pole' case passes on master apart from the new message assertion; only the synscan case reproduces the defect. Fine, but the header comment could say so.
- indigo_test/AGENTS.md asks forked-per-case suites to use integration/parallel_case_runner.h instead of a hand-written fork() loop; neighbouring agent suites also use their own loops, so not blocking.

notes.text: Owner decision (2026-11-19): the agent-side fix is not the right solution. The systemic way for a mount driver to publish coordinates from its position poll is indigo_update_coordinates(); that function is the single place that must handle 'the property is ALERT and has to stay ALERT'. A mount driver whose poll does not publish through indigo_update_coordinates() is defective. Survey: mount_synscan publishes MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES from the poll with indigo_update_property() and never calls indigo_update_coordinates(); ioptron, lx200, nexstar, nexstaraux, pmc8, rainbow, starbook, temma set OK in the driver before publishing; mount_simulator leaves the state alone.

Owner (2026-11-19): the second step, after ticket 9fe7f46e-cf10-4f1e-8b3a-cca9aa1f16f1 (mount_synscan poll through indigo_update_coordinates()), is to add a flag at the level of indigo_mount_driver that says whether an ALERT in the coordinates is to be kept or not; indigo_update_coordinates() honours it. To be registered as its own ticket when the first step is finished; design details (who sets and who clears the flag) to be agreed with the owner then.

Owner (2026-11-19) on the second step: the keep-ALERT flag is cleared only by the next request to move the mount; it has to be thought through what all of those requests are. Candidates to verify against the code when the ticket is written (coordinator's list, not the owner's): MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES in SLEW/TRACK mode, MOUNT_HORIZONTAL_COORDINATES, MOUNT_MOTION_RA / MOUNT_MOTION_DEC, MOUNT_PARK (park and unpark), MOUNT_HOME, driver-specific motion such as X_MOUNT_AUTOHOME, MOUNT_TRACKING on, MOUNT_ABORT_MOTION. Open points for the owner: whether a later SYNC (not a motion) that the mount accepts clears the flag, whether motion started outside INDIGO (hand controller, seen by the poll as BUSY) clears it, guide pulses, and disconnect/reconnect.

Owner (2026-11-19) on the second step: the keep-ALERT flag and the ALERT are cancelled by the BUSY state (seen in indigo_update_coordinates()), not by enumerating motion requests. A sync should publish BUSY too, because it is communication over the serial line and can take long; then an accepted sync after a refused one clears the flag the same way (BUSY, then OK), and a refused one ends BUSY -> ALERT with the flag set again. To verify when the ticket is written: which drivers already publish BUSY for a sync and which answer it without BUSY (including the base-driver alignment-point path used by mount_synscan and mount_simulator), and that the Mount Agent's wait for BUSY then also sees a sync.

questions.text: Design proposal for the second step (sync publishes BUSY, keep-ALERT flag), for the owner's decision before implementation. (1) Flag: one bool in the mount context of indigo_mount_driver, handled only inside indigo_update_coordinates(): when the function is called with the coordinates in BUSY it clears the flag; when it is called with ALERT while the previously published state was BUSY (a request or a motion ended in failure) it sets the flag; while the flag is set, a call with OK is published as ALERT. An ALERT that does not follow BUSY (a failed position readback in the poll) does not set the flag, so the next good poll restores OK as today. No driver sets or clears the flag itself. Open: (1a) refusals that never publish BUSY (parked mount through INDIGO_REJECT_CHANGE_IF, rainbow while homing, lx200 'Classic guiding is active') do not pass through indigo_update_coordinates() and would not be kept unless they are routed through it or the rule becomes 'every ALERT published with a message is kept'; (1b) should the flag also be cleared on disconnect. (2) Sync with BUSY for mount_synscan and mount_simulator (non-CONTROLLER alignment): their on_change_request delegates the sync to indigo_mount_change_property(), which answers synchronously without BUSY and publishes itself. Proposal: split the SYNC branch of indigo_mount_change_property() into a public helper (e.g. indigo_mount_sync(device), returning success and setting ALERT plus message on refusal, without publishing), have the two drivers take the generated path (INDIGO_COPY_*_PROCESS_CHANGE publishes BUSY, mount_equatorial_coordinates_handler calls the helper, the generated indigo_update_coordinates() publishes the result once); the refusal message is sent with indigo_send_message as in mount_starbook. indigo_mount_change_property() keeps the branch for drivers that still call it. Open: (2a) is changing the library API this way acceptable, or should the handler call indigo_mount_change_property() and the duplicate publication be removed differently. (3) Other deviations from the survey (temma sync completed by the finalizer, lx200 refusal exit, synscan GoTo ALERT exits using INDIGO_UPDATE_PROPERTY_STATE and return, generator parked guard publishing directly): fix them in this series or separately?

questions.text: Gap found in the step-2 design before implementation started (nothing implemented yet). The proposal said indigo_update_coordinates() clears the keep-ALERT flag when it is called with BUSY. It is never called with BUSY for a request: the generated change branch publishes BUSY with indigo_update_property() inside INDIGO_COPY_TARGETS_PROCESS_CHANGE (indigo_bus.h), and the handler is queued behind the poll on the same queue. Inside indigo_update_coordinates() a poll publishing OK after a refused request and a handler publishing OK for the next accepted sync look identical, so with the function alone an accepted sync after a refused one would be published as ALERT. Something has to tell the mount library that a new request was accepted. Options: (A) generator: for MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES the change branch publishes BUSY through indigo_update_coordinates() instead of indigo_update_property() (new macro or one generated line after the copy; indigo_tools/indigo_generator.c near line 2121); the function then really sees BUSY, clears the flag, and MOUNT_HORIZONTAL_COORDINATES follows BUSY as well; the ten generated mount drivers are regenerated, versions bumped where behaviour changes, off-limits mount_asi/mount_mxhd untouched and keep today's behaviour. (B) no generator change: indigo_mount_attach() wraps the device's change_property and clears the flag when a MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES request arrives while the property is not BUSY; hidden indirection in the base driver. (C) the handler's first call after a request is recognised by a per-request marker set by the driver; contradicts the rule that no driver handles the flag. Coordinator recommends (A). Generator changes need the owner's explicit approval of the concrete change.
